findings.issue: The new Application contention tests rely on a ten-second whole-child watchdog, but that helper stops enforcing a deadline when cleanup begins. The timeout branch calls blocking Child::wait with no bound; FixtureChild::drop also always waits without a bound after ignoring kill failure. If termination/reaping fails or stalls, timeout or inspection-error unwinding can hang the test runner rather than fail within a bounded fixture lifetime. In particular, shutdown_tests.rs deliberately awaits the original shutdown future after its500ms observation timeout, making the claimed whole-child lifetime essential to regression safety.
findings.recommendation: Give the service fixture one explicit bounded termination/reap path used by normal timeout, observation errors and Drop/unwind. Do not enter an unbounded wait after failed termination, do not silently detach owned work, and surface cleanup failure separately from the primary fixture failure with enough retained ownership information for explicit cleanup. Add deterministic fault-path verification for timeout/termination or inspection failure, preserving actual child/worker ownership, the original250ms/zero budgets and the new tests real joins. Do not fix this with a wider watchdog or a retry-to-green loop.
